questions.explain: The chapter's production-grade idle definition combines four signals over a rolling 7-day window: DatabaseConnections (avg < 2), CPUUtilization (< 1%), combined ReadIOPS + WriteIOPS (< 1), and NetworkReceiveThroughput (< 10 KB/s) — connection count alone produces false positives from pools and monitoring agents.
options: Zero connections in the last hour
Four signals over a 7-day window: connections < 2, CPU < 1%, combined IOPS < 1, network throughput < 10 KB/s
Any instance with less than 10 GB of storage
An instance whose CPU spiked above 90% once this week
questions.q: What is the chapter's production-grade definition of an 'idle' database instance?

questions.explain: Score 4 = STOP_OR_TERMINATE; score 3 = INVESTIGATE_THEN_STOP (notify owner with metrics evidence, no automated action for 7 days); score 2 = SCHEDULE_REVIEW. Re-check tags at action time for defense-in-depth.
options: Score 4 = notify, score 3 = terminate immediately, score 2 = ignore
Score 4 = stop; everything else is ignored
Score 4 = STOP_OR_TERMINATE; score 3 = INVESTIGATE_THEN_STOP (notify owner, no automated action for 7 days); score 2 = SCHEDULE_REVIEW
Scores are informational; all idle instances are terminated immediately
questions.q: How does the idle_score (0–4) map to recommended actions?

questions.explain: Three checks before shutdown: (1) recent snapshot/backup activity (a snapshot within 48 hours may indicate an active pipeline), (2) tag-based exemptions re-verified at action time (AutoShutdown=false, Environment=production, etc.), and (3) cross-reference with application deployment records (CMDB/Resource Graph) so databases linked to active apps go back to the team for confirmation.
options: Check backup recency, verify tag exemptions at action time, and cross-reference with application deployment records
Check only the instance name for the word 'test'
Verify the AWS region is us-east-1
No validation is needed if the idle score is 4
questions.q: What are the three validation checks required before any shutdown action?

questions.explain: Stop preserves configuration and backups; compute billing stops but storage keeps billing, and AWS auto-restarts stopped instances after 7 days (saving ~60–70% of the bill). Terminate with final snapshot ends compute and storage billing entirely, with snapshot storage at $0.095/GB-month — the right choice for confirmed decommissions.
options: There is no difference; both delete the instance
Stop is permanent, terminate is reversible
Terminate keeps storage billing, stop does not
Stop saves compute (but storage keeps billing and AWS restarts after 7 days); terminate with final snapshot ends all ongoing costs
questions.q: What is the difference between Stop and Terminate for an idle instance?

questions.explain: Common failure modes: read replicas can't be stopped independently while the primary is running (stop replicas first, then the primary); stopping saves compute/license but not storage; Multi-AZ stop causes brief failover; snapshots must complete before deletion (poll/wait); and CloudWatch alarms need treat-missing-data notBreaching so already-stopped instances stay quiet.
options: There are no failure modes; shutdown automation is always safe
Read replicas cannot be stopped independently of the primary — stop replicas first, then the primary; also stopping does not save storage, and snapshots must complete before deletion
Only the cost of the snapshot
The 7-day auto-restart can be disabled via a tag
